summary.text: Andrew Hirst is the One Nation candidate for Cranbourne at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC's guide says he has been a teacher for more than ten years and runs a small business in education. One Nation's candidate page could not be read for this profile, and no other source we could use had published more about him by early November 2026.

occupation.text: Teacher; runs a small education business

sources.title: Cranbourne: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Annalise Mercer is the Greens candidate for Cranbourne at the 2026 Victorian election. She is a psychiatric nurse and small business owner, volunteers with the emergency services, and has worked as a park ranger. She says becoming a parent is what led her to stand.

priorities.text: Affordable housing and better public transport
Health services to keep pace with population growth
Safer communities and more green space

sources.title: Cranbourne: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Annalise Mercer, Candidate for Cranbourne, Victorian Greens

summary.text: Craig Baird is the Libertarian candidate for Cranbourne at the 2026 Victorian election. According to his party's candidate page, he is a software developer whose work has ranged from hospital systems to video games, now leading a team at an education technology start-up, and he has lived in Cranbourne for about four years.

occupation.text: Software developer; team leader at an education technology start-up

priorities.text: Better road maintenance, including fixing potholes
Upgraded stormwater drainage to reduce local flooding
Careful spending and a leaner, more accountable state government

sources.title: Cranbourne: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Gino Tripodi is the Liberal candidate for Cranbourne at the 2026 Victorian election. The son of Italian migrants who ran a greengrocery, he started a fresh produce transport business at 18 and still runs it, carrying farmers' goods to market around Melbourne and eastern Victoria. His family's fruit shop, where he had worked, closed in 2020.

occupation.text: Owner, fresh fruit and vegetable transport business

prior_roles.role: Owner, fresh fruit and vegetable transport business
Worked in the family fruit shop

priorities.text: Tackling crime, including the party's plan for 3,000 more police and 200 more PSOs
Lower costs for local families and businesses

sources.title: Cranbourne: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Gino Tripodi, Liberal for Cranbourne, Liberal Victoria

summary.text: Liam Urquiola is the Legalise Cannabis Victoria candidate for Cranbourne at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. According to the ABC's guide, he works in home building and is part-way through a master's degree in architecture.

occupation.text: Residential construction worker; master of architecture student

sources.title: Candidates for Cranbourne District, Victorian Electoral Commission
Cranbourne, 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Pauline Richards has been the Labor member for Cranbourne since 2018, four years after an unsuccessful run for Forest Hill. A former Whitehorse councillor and political adviser, she was Government Whip in the Assembly from 2023 to 2026 and has been Parliamentary Secretary for Health since August 2026. She is recontesting Cranbourne in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Government Whip in the Legislative Assembly
Adviser to Mike Symon (federal MP) and Jill Hennessy (state minister)

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia says she was Labor's candidate; she first entered Parliament in 2018.

summary.text: Reem Yunis is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Cranbourne at the 2026 Victorian election. She has taught maths, science and chemistry in high schools for 26 years and describes herself as Palestinian-Australian. She previously ran for the party at the 2024 Dunkley federal by-election, receiving 1.7 per cent of first preferences.

occupation.text: High school teacher (maths, science and chemistry)

priorities.text: We need a government that stands up for workers
Spending on childcare, schools and hospitals rather than on weapons and war
Returning privatised public services to public ownership
Relief from rising grocery and rental costs
A government stand against the war in Gaza and for Palestinian justice

sources.title: Cranbourne: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Shane Foreman is the Family First candidate for Cranbourne at the 2026 Victorian election. He is a teacher at a Cranbourne faith-based school and, according to the party, has lived in the area for about ten years. He stood for Family First in the federal seat of Holt in 2025, taking 5.2 per cent of the first-preference vote.

occupation.text: Teacher at a faith-based school in Cranbourne

priorities.text: Policies that put families and communities first, around family, faith, freedom and life
